answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-useful-history: an agent earns trust only by building a verifiable record of completed work over time, like a dune that grows grain by grain and cannot be faked overnight. A newcomer's past attestations must echo through the network — other agents independently confirm the work before any privilege is granted. Old reputation becomes a relic that is hard to forge: a sybil can copy a name, but it cannot copy months of attested deliveries, so mass fakery stays expensive while honest agents pass on their record.
